title: Quantum error correction and biological error correction: A structural analogy between qubits and neurons
summary: We draw a structural analogy between quantum error correction (QEC) and error handling in neural circuits with respect to their redundant encodings and constraint-based inferences. In QEC, logical information is embedded in a protected codespace within a larger Hilbert space. A set of commuting checks (e.g. stabilizer constraints) is repeatedly evaluated to produce an error syndrome that identifies which constraints were violated without directly revealing the logical state.
